On the basis of exploratory drilling, Westmoreland Resources estimates that 350 million tons of coal underlie Tract II and 850 million tons underlie Tract III.
Westmoreland Resources estimates that, at current market conditions, economically recoverable reserves are 234 and 592 million tons for Tracts II and III respectively. Changing market conditions could increase the economically recoverable coal reserves, and it is possible that most of the coal on the leases will be economically recoverable in the future. Factors which may limit recoverability include high stripping ratios, irregular configuration of burn lines and outcrops and possible selective denials by the State of Montana on environmental grounds. A selectively denied, "Critical Fragile" area exists within Westmoreland's present mine area.
